newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hoechst makes buyout bid for Roussel.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst makes buyout bid for Roussel.

text.p: Societe Francaise Hoechst, majority shareholder in Roussel Uclaf, said on Wednesday that it had offered to buy out minority shareholders in the French pharmaceuticals group for 1,530 francs per ordinary share and 1,330 francs per preference share.
This values the buyout offer at a total 18.1 billion francs ($3.5 billion), Hoechst said in a statement.
ERAP, the second largest shareholder in Roussel after Hoechst with 4.28 percent of Roussel's capital, has indicated that it will tender its shares in the offer. ($ = 5.225 French Francs)
Erap "has indicated it will tender its shares in the offer," Hoechst said in the statement.
The offer sets a 12 percent premium on the average price of the common stock over the previous month and 19 percent over the average price over the previous three months, Hoechst said.
SBC Warburg has made a valuation on the fair value of the offer and submitted its study to the board of Roussel, Hoechst said.

Following the present offer, if Hoechst acquires at least 95 percent of Roussel's voting rights, it plans to launch a public offer to withdraw the remaining shares, priced on the same tersms as the buyout.
Roussel Uclaf expects to undertake 220 million francs of financing on various research programmes with public authorities. It will continue to run the research centre at Romainville, Hoechst said.
